sections.h2: What makes property tax in Casey County, Kentucky different?
sections.html:
The yearly rhythm matches the rest of Kentucky: the PVA values property as of January 1, the sheriff collects from early October until April 15, and the county clerk picks up what remains. The difference is the setting. Casey County spreads over about 446 square miles with only one city, Liberty, and the 2020 census counted every resident as rural.

That shapes bills in practice. Almost every parcel is a farm tract, a hillside lot in the Knobs or a house on one of the state routes crossing the county, so the assessed value is the first number to examine before you list.

sections.h2: Which Casey County office handles which tax question?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA about value, the sheriff about what you owe this year, and the clerk about anything delinquent. The offices below are the ones the county's own pages list.

sections.h2: What is the Casey County housing picture?
sections.html:
Small, spread out and mostly owned by the people who live in it. Lincoln County gave up its western portion to form Casey in 1806, and the courthouse in Liberty dates from 1888. The 2020 census recorded 15,941 residents in 6,270 households and 7,366 housing units, 14.9 percent of them vacant. Roughly 76 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied, so many sellers are parting with the home they live in.

Wikipedia describes Casey as the only Kentucky county lying wholly in the Knobs, with its high point at Green River Knob, 1,789 feet. Hillside access, wells, septic systems and road frontage are worth documenting before you list. US 127, KY 80 and KY 49 are among the roads serving the county, and Casey County Schools operates the public schools. The annual Casey County Apple Festival is the county's signature event.

  • Neighbors are Boyle, Lincoln, Pulaski, Russell, Adair, Taylor and Marion counties.
  • Russell and Adair mark a time zone boundary to the south and southwest.
  • With Liberty the lone city, only in-town homes raise city tax questions.

sections.h2: How do Casey County payment dates and penalties work?
sections.html:
The sheriff's bill sets the amount, and the payment date moves the total. KRS 134.015 gives a 2 percent discount for full payment through November 1, the bill amount from November 2 to December 31, a 5 percent penalty during January, and a 10 percent penalty starting February 1, with the sheriff's add-on fee on top.

The lien from an unpaid bill stays on the parcel for eleven years, whoever holds title. If collection starts late in a given year, the Department of Revenue can substitute a schedule that gives owners 30 days at each stage.

Lost the bill? Get the parcel number from the PVA or clerk and ask the sheriff for a copy. Mortgage escrow payments still leave the bill in your name, so confirm the payment posted before closing.

sections.h2: How can I contest a Casey County valuation?
sections.html:
Ask the Casey County PVA for a conference while the tax roll is open to public viewing, a thirteen-day stretch that starts the first Monday of May. A phone conference is allowed on request.

When that fails, mail or deliver a written petition to the county clerk by the workday after the viewing period ends, with the parcel, your reasons and your opinion of fair cash value. A hearing follows about a month later. Evidence carries the day: sales of similar houses, construction cost records, an insurance policy or a recent appraisal. Under KRS 133.120 the board denies an appeal if the owner will not hand over reasonable value information when asked.

  • Hold the PVA conference first, because skipping it closes later doors.
  • Keep paying on the value you claimed while the case is pending.
  • A raised value brings a supplemental bill that is due the day it is prepared.

sections.h2: How does the Casey County delinquent tax sale work?
sections.html:
After April 15 an unpaid bill goes to the clerk and can be sold to a private buyer at an annual sale. For the 2025 bills, the Casey County Clerk received the sheriff's list on April 16, 2026, ran the notice in The Casey County News on July 15, 2026, and set the sale for Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9:00 am in its office on Campbellsville Street. Those dates are behind us, and each year's sale follows a similar summer pattern.

Owners can pay up to the moment the sale opens. Bidders register with the clerk ten days ahead and pay a recording fee of $46 per lien assignment, as the clerk's page lists. Buying more than three certificates in a county, or more than five statewide, also requires registration with the Department of Revenue.

The sale itself runs like a draft. Registered buyers draw numbers at random, then take turns picking certificates from the lists they filed, and for the 2026 sale the clerk planned one certificate per round because of the volume. The clerk's office tells buyers it will not research bills for them, so a parcel with a problem such as a bankruptcy filing is the buyer's risk. Once someone buys your certificate, you owe that buyer and fees can grow. Paying earlier prevents it.

sections.h2: Does Casey County have tax relief for older or disabled owners?
sections.html:
Yes, through the state homestead exemption for owners in their retirement years or with a total disability. A fixed dollar amount comes off the home's assessed value. The Department of Revenue set it at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 and publishes a new amount every second year. File with the Casey County PVA and bring proof such as a driver's license or passport.

The relief belongs to the owner who lives in the house. If you move into care or sell partway through the year, tell the PVA so the next bill reflects it.

sections.h2: How do I close a Casey County sale when tax is unpaid?
sections.html:
Collect written balances from the clerk and the sheriff and hand them to the closing agent. Anything unpaid at the table comes out of your price, and a lien the clerk filed must be released before the buyer takes clean title. Releases are recorded at the clerk's office for a posted fee.

For an inherited, empty or worn-down house, a cash buyer that takes the property as is can pay the tax from the price. That keeps your parcel off the August list, where delinquent bills become public.

faqs.q: Where do I find my Casey County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Ask the Casey County sheriff's office, which sends the bills. If you lack its number, the clerk at 606-787-6471 or the PVA at 606-787-7621 can point you to it and help identify your parcel.

faqs.q: When was the 2026 Casey County tax sale?
faqs.a: It was set for Friday, August 14, 2026 at 9:00 am at the clerk's office, 625 Campbellsville Street in Liberty. Owners could pay their unpaid 2025 bills up to the start of the sale.

faqs.q: How big is the homestead exemption for Casey County owners?
faqs.a: The state figure was $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, subtracted from the assessed value. It is open to owners 65 and up or totally disabled, and you apply through the Casey County PVA.

faqs.q: Is it too late to appeal if I missed the May viewing period?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The PVA conference and the clerk filing both fall inside that window, unless the state approved an extension of up to 25 days. Ask the PVA whether one applied.

faqs.q: Does unpaid tax stop me from selling Casey County land?
faqs.a: No. The bill and any lien get cleared at closing from your proceeds. Ask the sheriff or clerk for payoff amounts first so the title company can deduct them.
